title: TTFT guardrails and streaming multiplexing checklist
text:
TTFT guardrails and streaming multiplexing checklist

['From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@fastorder.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT guardrails and streaming multiplexing checklist

Emma — thanks for the call earlier. Quick written recap + asks so we have alignment before engineering sync.

Key decisions we captured:
- TTFT targets: median ~120–150ms for initial chunk (warm), p95 <= 400ms for early partial emit.
- Throughput/concurrency: pilot expected ~200 RPS peak, concurrency per instance ~50 concurrent streams.
- Preferred streaming mode: SSE preferred for server-initiated partials, but WebSocket fallback required for mobile clients that need connection multiplexing.
- Chunk cadence: target ~40–120ms inter-chunk spacing under normal conditions; allow batching into 200–300ms windows under burst.
- Multiplexing: need ability to multiplex multiple logical chats over a single WS connection for mobile; SSE will be single-stream per connection.

Immediate open technical questions for your team (please confirm):
1) Are you able to accept SSE with TLS termination at our edge? If not, we’ll enable WS with proxy-friendly headers.
2) Do you need per-endpoint API key rotation (we can support short-lived tokens + JWKS)?
3) Any constraints on chunk size (max bytes per chunk) for your mobile clients?

Attached: quick results from our lab probe (ttft_probe_results.csv) and a handshake diagram (streaming-handshake-diagram.png).

Proposed next steps:
- Emma/fastorder: confirm answers to the 3 questions above by EOD Monday (14 Sep).
- Redwood: run a synthetic probe with WS multiplexing option on Tuesday and share latency traces.
- Schedule a 30m tech sync (engineering + mobile architect) — proposed Wed 15 Sep 10:00 PT.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate dates once you confirm.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:01:23 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT guardrails and streaming multiplexing checklist

Thanks for the clear recap, Jonas — appreciate it. Quick answers from our side:
- TLS termination: we prefer TLS end-to-end; if Redwood terminates at the edge that's OK provided mutual TLS is supported for the pilot.
- API keys: we do short-lived keys today; JWKS rotation is preferred.
- Chunk size: on iOS Android we’d like chunks <= 8KB to avoid reassembly issues on poor networks. If you can cap chunk payloads, that would be ideal.

Also: our mobile team strongly prefers WebSocket multiplexing because we already multiplex notifications and streams in the same connection. I attached a small proto file showing how we currently namespace streams (mobile-proto.json).

We’re good to do Wed 15 Sep 10:00 PT for the tech sync — added mobile-arch to CC.

Emma Liu
Senior Product Manager, Integrations
FastOrder Inc.
emma.liu@fastorder.com

To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: TTFT guardrails and streaming multiplexing checklist (internal)

Looping in a couple internal notes before sync so we don’t surprise the customer.
- If FastOrder requires WS multiplexing, we should propose two fallback policies:
  * Policy A (conservative): prefer SSE, fallback to WS without multiplexing when SSE unsupported.
  * Policy B (mobile-friendly): support WS multiplexing with per-logical-stream token and enforce <=8KB chunk payloads.
- For TTFT targets we can meet median 120–150ms in warmstart for the pilot with current model selection; p95 ~380–420ms when we enable prefix caching. We should capture traces for both: warm-cache and cold-start.
- Canary config suggestion: run 10% traffic to multiplexing-enabled nodes for 48 hours, measure p50/p95 and memory v. CPU delta.
- Infra ask: can ops provision a small 4-GPU pool pre-warmed with the model variant used in the probe by Tue EOD? That will be needed to replicate numbers.

I’ll prepare a short runbook to share in the tech sync (will include suggested circuit-breaker thresholds and retry windows).

—
Priyom Das
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference', 'From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@fastorder.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, mobile-arch@fastorder.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT guardrails and streaming multiplexing checklist — action items

Thanks everyone — good sync this morning. Finalized action items and owners below.

Action items (owners / target):
1) FastOrder (Emma + mobile-arch): confirm TLS + mutual TLS details and share any network egress whitelist by EOD 17 Sep. (Emma)
2) Redwood infra: provision 4x GPU pool pre-warmed with the probe model; run WS multiplexing synthetic probe (Priyom) — deliver traces by 18 Sep.
3) Redwood eng (Jonas): implement chunk-size cap at 8KB on WS path and add header X-Stream-Id for per-logical-stream routing — PR by 20 Sep.
4) Both teams: 30m tech sync to run through handshake and token rotation flow — follow-up meeting invite (scheduled).

Notes: we agreed to use Policy B for the pilot (WS multiplexing enabled, chunk limit 8KB, per-stream short-lived tokens). We will monitor p50/p95, error-rate and CPU/memory per node during the canary.

Next meeting: calendar invite sent for Thu 16 Sep 10:00 PT (engineering + mobile architecture). If anything changes, reply-all.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
